Design System

Cuttlefish Design Library

Building the Foundation for Clinician-Facing Products

Role
Senior UX/UI Designer
Type
Design System
Scale
90+ Components
Status
Active · In Production

Overview

The Challenge

Clinician-facing applications at Optum were growing quickly across multiple product teams, but without a shared design foundation, inconsistencies in UI patterns, spacing, and interactions were adding friction for both designers and developers.

We needed a single source of truth: a robust, scalable design library that teams could build on confidently, and that would hold up under the complexity of real clinical workflows.

Key Goals

01

Create a shared visual language across all clinician-facing products

02

Reduce design and development time through reusable, well-documented components

03

Ensure accessibility and consistency across all states, variants, and breakpoints

04

Build something teams would actually want to use, practical, flexible, and easy to adopt

Constraints

Building With a Small Team

The library was built and maintained by just two designers while several product teams were already mid build on the old system. With no dedicated engineering team for the design system itself, everything had to be migratable rather than a clean slate rebuild.

The Library

90+ Components, Built to Last

Working closely with one other designer, I contributed to building Cuttlefish from the ground up, covering everything from foundational tokens and typography to complex interactive patterns used throughout clinical workflows.

Every component was designed with multiple states, variants, and edge cases in mind. We documented usage guidelines, accessibility requirements, and interaction specs so that any team could pick up and build with confidence.

Trade-offs

Alternatives Considered

01

Rebuild everything, or migrate gradually?

We considered a full breaking rebuild, but chose incremental token and component migration instead. In flight teams didn't have to stall, though it meant running two systems in parallel longer than we would have liked.

02

Maximum flexibility, or an opinionated set of variants?

We considered maximizing configurability for every component, but chose a smaller, more opinionated set of variants. That kept the library documentable by two people, at the cost of some one off flexibility teams asked for.

03

Mandate adoption, or earn it?

We considered mandating adoption top down, but chose to earn it by making the library easier to use than the alternative. It took longer to reach full adoption, but the usage that resulted was genuine.

Impact

Now the Standard at Optum

Cuttlefish is the active design library powering all clinician-facing applications at Optum. What started as a solution to inconsistency became the shared foundation every product team builds on.

01
Adopted as the single design system for all clinician-facing products, eliminating inconsistency across teams and product lines.
02
Accelerated design and development cycles by giving teams a ready-made, well-documented component library to build from rather than from scratch.
03
Raised the accessibility and interaction quality baseline across the portfolio, every component ships with full state coverage, ARIA guidance, and responsive behavior.
04
Still actively maintained and expanded, Cuttlefish continues to grow as new clinical workflows require new patterns.
